A landlord who has reported the required information about their rental unit to the Rent
Board as set forth in Section 37.15 shall have a license to impose annually a rent increase which
does not exceed a tenant's base rent by more than 60% of said published increase. In no event,
however, shall the allowable annual increase be greater than 7%.
results.plain_language: Landlords may only increase rent once per year by up to 60% of the regional CPI increase, capped at an absolute maximum of 7%. Unused increases may be banked and imposed on subsequent anniversary dates.

results.quoted_span:
Where a landlord seeks eviction based upon

Section 37.9(a)(13), and the notice of intent to withdraw rental units is filed with the Rent Board

on or after September 1, 2022, the landlord shall pay relocation payments in the manner

described in Subsection 37.9A(e)(1)(A) and (B), except that the specific amount of the relocation

benefit shall be $10,000 per Eligible Tenant, and the total relocation payment shall be $30,000 in

the event there are more than three Eligible Tenants in the unit; and further, an Eligible Tenant

who meets any of the criteria listed in Subsection 37.9A(e)(1)(C) shall be entitled to receive an

additional payment of $6,700, in two payments of $3,350 each, the timing of which is set forth in

that subsection.
results.conflict_reason: superseded by: both in force, city rule displaces city rule
results.plain_language: Landlords withdrawing units from the rental market under the Ellis Act must provide statutory relocation payments per eligible tenant (with extra payments for seniors or disabled tenants) and comply with strict re-rental and rent restrictions if the units are returned to the rental market within 5 to 10 years.
results.plain_language_es: Los propietarios que retiran unidades del mercado de alquiler bajo la Ley Ellis deben proporcionar pagos legales de reubicación por inquilino elegible (con pagos adicionales para personas de la tercera edad o con discapacidades) y cumplir con estrictas restricciones de re-alquiler y límites de renta si las unidades vuelven a ofrecerse en alquiler dentro de 5 a 10 años.

all rights under any other provision of law, shall be entitled to receive relocation expenses from

results.conflict_reason: superseded by: both in force, city rule displaces city rule
results.plain_language: Eligible tenants who receive a covered no-fault eviction notice (such as owner/relative move-in, capital improvements, or substantial rehabilitation) are entitled to statutory relocation expenses, including an additional payment for senior, disabled, or household occupants with minor children.

results.quoted_span:
Any residential tenant who was in possession of a rental unit at the time of

foreclosure may not be evicted by the person or entity who took title through foreclosure (see

Section 37.9D(a)), except for just cause as provided in Section 37.9 and related provisions of

Chapter 37, or at the end of the tenant's existing lease, whichever occurs later.
results.conflict_reason: superseded by: both in force, city rule displaces city rule
results.plain_language: Tenants occupying a rental unit at the time of foreclosure cannot be evicted by the successor owner who took title through foreclosure without just cause under Section 37.9 or before the expiration of their existing lease, whichever is later, and must be provided written notice of their rights within 15 days.
results.plain_language_es: Los inquilinos que ocupen una unidad al momento de una ejecución hipotecaria no pueden ser desalojados por el nuevo titular que obtuvo la propiedad tras la ejecución, salvo por causa justificada bajo la Sección 37.9 o al finalizar el contrato de arrendamiento existente (lo que ocurra más tarde), y deben recibir notificación por escrito de sus derechos dentro de 15 días.

results.quoted_span:
Consistent with Section 37.9(a)(2) and

Section 37.9(e), any provision of any lease or rental agreement that purports to require a tenant

to vacate a rental unit at the expiration of a stated term, or that purports to characterize a

tenant’s failure to vacate the rental unit at the end of the stated term as a just cause for eviction

(either of them, a “Fixed-Term Agreement”), shall be void as contrary to public policy, and a

landlord may not attempt to recover possession of the unit without just cause.
results.conflict_reason: superseded by: both in force, city rule displaces city rule
results.plain_language: Lease provisions requiring a tenant to vacate at the end of a stated term or classifying failure to vacate at term expiration as just cause for eviction are void as contrary to public policy, unless Chapter 37 expressly authorizes a fixed term.
results.plain_language_es: Las disposiciones contractuales que exigen que un inquilino desocupe la unidad al vencer un plazo fijo o que califiquen la falta de desocupación como justa causa de desalojo son nulas por ser contrarias al orden público, salvo que el Capítulo 37 autorice expresamente dicho plazo fijo.

removed by the Superior Court from any house, building, mobile home or land in a mobile home park or
tenement leased for residential purposes, other than (1) owner-occupied premises with not more than two
rental units or a hotel, motel or other guest house or part thereof rented to a transient guest or seasonal
tenant; (2) a dwelling unit which is held in trust on behalf of a member of the immediate family of the person
or persons establishing the trust, provided that the member of the immediate family on whose behalf the
trust is established permanently occupies the unit; and (3) a dwelling unit which is permanently occupied by
a member of the immediate family of the owner of that unit, provided, however, that exception (2) or (3)
shall apply only in cases in which the member of the immediate family has a developmental disability,
except upon establishment of one of the following grounds as good cause:
results.plain_language: Landlords cannot remove a residential tenant except by establishing one of the statutory good-cause grounds specified by law.
results.plain_language_es: Los arrendadores no pueden desalojar a un inquilino residencial excepto si demuestran una de las causas justificadas establecidas por la ley.
